mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates a strengthening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of overall economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the periods following a sustained 3-month increase in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals an improving labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side, which increases corporate earnings and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than GDP (GDPC1) over a 3-month period, it indicates a consumer-driven demand surge, which is likely to lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > GDPC1 growth over 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3% each in a single month signals a robust labor market, which boosts economic activity and thus positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 0.3% and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of the periods following a sustained 3-month increase in CPIAUCSL by more than 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in real GDP (GDPC1) is negative, it signals a contraction in economic activity, which is likely to lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances when the trigger condition is met.
